issues.where: 12-lead ECG, V4–V6 column (x≈1683–1905, y≈85–460), 52 s frame
issues.problem: The leads do not match the rhythm strip at the same moments. On the strip below, the shock is at x≈1693 and everything to its right is post-shock sinus (ticks 1,483 and 833). The V4–V6 column covers the same 7.5–10 s window but still shows large sinusoidal VT waves all the way to the right edge. So the top rows and the strip disagree about the rhythm at the same instant. This undercuts the cause-and-effect claim of the piece, and anyone who reads ECGs will spot it.
issues.fix: Write all 12 lead buffers from the same sample index and sweep position as the lead II strip, and don't skip or freeze any column after the shock or during blanking. Check this by drawing the SHOCK marker in the V4–V6 column as well: it should sit at the same x as the strip marker.

issues.where: Whole page, frame timing (max 273 ms of JS in one frame)
issues.problem: A single frame takes 273 ms. In a 60 fps recording that shows as a visible freeze of about 16 frames, most likely at prewarm handoff, the S2 or the shock. That is exactly where the audience is watching.
issues.fix: Profile the spike. Move any one-off work (gain freeze, histogram rebuilds, beat-table reflow, worker result merge) out of the rAF callback, or spread it over several frames. Then check that the recorded run keeps max frame time under 33 ms.

issues.problem: The four-chamber slice fills only about 430×560 px of the hero tile, and the ventricular walls are about 20–25 px thick on screen. The reentry, which is the story, shows up as thin coloured bands that X's video compression will smear. The only place you can actually see the circuit round the scar is the 150 px 'SCAR CIRCUIT' inset. The lower-left and right areas of the hero (around 330–470 × 430–560 and 860–990 × 430–480) hold only scattered electrode labels.
issues.fix: Scale the slice so it fills the tile, about 640 px tall. Move the V1–V6 electrode badges onto a tighter arc around the heart. Enlarge the scar-circuit inset to about 240 px and place it in the freed lower-left corner, so the rotating wavefront and tip trail can be read at phone size.

issues.where: Hero, RA electrode callout (≈375–440, 207), 52 s frame
issues.problem: The 'SA' pacemaker label that appears after the shock collides with the 'RA iso' callout box (it reads 'RA iso )rSA'). Also, every electrode readout switches to the word 'iso' instead of a number, so the electrode potentials look like they are missing.
issues.fix: Offset the SA label below the RA wall marker, or give it a leader line. Always print the numeric potential (for example '+0.00 mV') and mark it isoelectric with colour, not by replacing the value with 'iso'.

issues.where: Event log, top row (y≈636), 19 s and 36 s frames
issues.problem: The oldest line is cut horizontally in half (for example 'PS −1 born at (385, 206)' shows only its lower half). It reads as clipped text rather than a deliberate fade.
issues.fix: Scroll the log by whole line heights, or put a 1-line gradient mask over a fully rendered row, so no glyph is cut through the middle.

issues.where: Heart-rate beat-by-beat chart (≈1704–1905, 615–740), 19 s and 36 s
issues.problem: The red VT trace at about 138 bpm runs straight through the '150' limit label at the right edge, and at 19 s the spike to 173 bpm touches the top of the chart.
issues.fix: Put the limit labels on the left end of the dashed lines or outside the plot area, and add 10% headroom to the y-range above the maximum HR.

issues.where: Beat table / log / rhythm strip around S2 (19 s frame)
issues.problem: The S2 premature beat is never detected. The beat after S2 is logged as '#29 WIDE RR 1086 HR 55', which makes VT onset look like a pause. VT is then declared at 'HR 173' from a single 346 ms interval, while the sustained VT runs at 436 ms / 138 bpm.
issues.fix: Detect the S2-driven complex, or annotate it explicitly as 'S2 capture, CI 320'. Declare VT only after 3 consecutive wide beats, and report the median rate of those beats in the 'VT detected' line and the header.

issues.where: Workstation GPU solver and header 'CELL UPD/S 42.8 M measured'
issues.problem: The value is exactly 42.76 M in every frame. That is 23,754 × 30 × 60 computed from nominal counts, but the label says 'measured'.
issues.fix: Compute it from actual substeps completed divided by the real elapsed time (rAF deltas or EXT_disjoint_timer_query) so it fluctuates realistically. Otherwise relabel it as 'nominal'.

issues.problem: It says (8) in every frame even though the table lists 17 or more sinus beats, and the values are identical before and after the shock. It is unclear which beats it averages.
issues.fix: Label it as a rolling window ('last 8 sinus') or make it a true running mean with the correct n. Split pre-VT and post-shock sinus if the row is meant to show recovery.

issues.where: ECG rhythm strip, caliper labels at right edge (≈1855–1900, 560–575), 2 s frame
issues.problem: The 'PR 194' and 'QRS 114' caliper labels are squeezed against the right border of the paper and partly run into the panel edge.
issues.fix: Anchor the caliper readouts to the left of the measured beat whenever it falls in the last 80 px of the strip.

critic.summary:
This is a strong, credible piece. The EP-lab design fits the brief: light clinical palette, pink millimetre ECG paper, monitor-style vitals and a dense, well-aligned bottom band. The four frames tell the whole story: sinus, then VT with AV dissociation, then the shock, then sinus again.

The numbers hold up under checking:
- RR matches HR, and Bazett QTc is correct.
- APD plus DI equals the cycle length at every probe (434 ms in VT, 833 ms in sinus).
- The restitution slope matches its fitted curve.
- Header countdowns agree with 0.46× playback.
- The shock timing on the strip matches 'delivered 6.5 s ago'.
- The mean anchored PS during VT is consistent with the frontal-axis arrow.

What must be fixed before posting:
- In the 52 s frame, the V4–V6 leads still show VT where the lead II strip shows post-shock sinus.
- One frame takes 273 ms, which will show as a visible stutter in the recording.

The biggest gap in impact is the hero: the slice is undersized and the walls are thin, so the reentry reads as thin bands. The circuit itself only shows clearly in a 150 px inset. Enlarging the heart and the scar inset would make this a stop-scrolling post. The remaining issues are small collisions and clipping (the SA label against 'RA iso', the half-cut log line, the HR chart's limit label) and a few labelling details: the S2 beat isn't detected, 'measured' is constant, and 'SINUS mean (8)' doesn't say which beats it averages.
